issues.description: Unbounded in-memory log buffer with no cap or eviction policy
issues.detail: _BufferingHandler.buffer is a plain list with no size limit. If a job hangs before init_recording or logs heavily during slow startup, memory grows without bound — a crash-log feature that OOMs the worker is worse than the bug it fixes. Use a bounded deque(maxlen=N) so the structure itself enforces the policy.

issues.description: Replay scans root handlers for OTLP LoggingHandler instead of holding a reference
issues.detail: _flush_early_log_buffer iterates logging.getLogger().handlers picking the first LoggingHandler match. If another subsystem installed an OTLP handler, the replay targets the wrong one and the real handler is skipped. _setup_cloud_tracer knows which handler it installed — store and pass that reference directly rather than guessing by isinstance walk.

issues.description: _shutdown_telemetry strips all LoggingHandlers from root logger as global side effect
issues.detail: The deadlock workaround removes every LoggingHandler from the root logger, not just the one this module installed. In embedding scenarios or multi-job hosts, this rips out handlers the user or other subsystems attached. Track the handler reference installed by _setup_cloud_tracer and detach only that one. Global mutation to fix a local problem is wrong scope.

issues.description: Makefile drops pytest-xdist parallelism and excludes google STT test without justification
issues.detail: The diff removes -n auto and skips test_plugin_google_stt.py with no commit rationale. This serializes CI for everyone and silently drops coverage. If xdist became flaky from the new global logger mutations, document it; if the test is broken, quarantine it explicitly. As-is it reads like a local workaround that escaped into main.

issues.description: Patch bundles three unrelated changes: crash-log upload, worker.py race fix, makefile test-infra
issues.detail: The worker.py reordering of _queue_msg vs pending_assignments registration is a real race fix, and the makefile changes are test infrastructure. Neither belongs in a patch titled around log upload. Split into separate commits so bisect and revert work cleanly, and add a one-line comment on the worker.py reorder so future readers don't undo it.

issues.description: Lifecycle methods and reentry paths need literate comments and audit trail
issues.detail: The four parallel buffer-lifecycle methods on JobContext could collapse into one LogBuffer object owning attach/detach/replay. The reentry path in _stop_log_buffering silently drops buffered records with no count logged, and the _shutdown_fut suppress(InvalidStateError) lacks an invariant comment. State the invariants and consolidate ownership.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the crash-log upload design is structurally sound — buffer early, replay through OTLP once recording initializes, force-resolve shutdown_fut on early crash — but execution has three concrete problems all reviewers flagged independently: an unbounded buffer list, replay-by-isinstance-walk instead of holding the handler reference, and _shutdown_telemetry mutating the global root logger to work around a local deadlock. Additionally the patch smuggles in unrelated worker.py race fixes and makefile test-infra regressions (dropped -n auto, skipped google STT test) with no commit rationale. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — scope the handler ownership, cap the buffer, split the patch, and explain the makefile changes before merge.
